clearedSpotChecks.check: Task 2, rerun of a seeded sample of the Algebra swaps (alg19.py): 22,560 of 22,560 swaps reproduce to the unit, 3,846 reach the 512 bit branch of mulDiv and 2,879 need it.
clearedSpotChecks.note: out/algB-summary.json holds ok 22560 of 22560, empty mismatches and groupErrors, and the four algB-*.mismatch.jsonl files have 0 lines, while the pass 1 files alg-[0-3].mismatch.jsonl hold 31+46+42+25 = 144 lines as stated. I recomputed 48 needBranch swaps (40 drawn with random.Random(7) from algB-0, algB-2 and algB-3, plus every swap of two multi-swap blocks) with my own exact Python integer arithmetic, not v4math.py: parent-block globalState() (0xe76c01e4) and liquidity() (0x1a686502) read by eth_call on https://rpc.purroofgroup.com (web3_clientVersion reth/v0.1.0-f0cad31), the Swap log read by eth_getTransactionReceipt and eth_getLogs, then amountAfterFee = amount0*(1e6-fee)/1e6, the rounded-up price of getNextSqrtPriceFromAmount0RoundingUp and amount1 = L*(P-Pn)/2^96 rounded down, each swap chained from the previous Swap log of the same pool and block. All 48 match liquidity, price and amount1 to the unit. The products involved exceed 256 bits, so the chain's MULMOD and DIV results on the 512 bit path of src/libraries/FullMath.sol:14-116 agree with exact math on these swaps. The two that failed my first pass were later swaps in a block whose earlier swaps I had not applied; chained, they match. One trap for other units: https://rpc.hyperliquid.xyz/evm, the URL in state/networks.json, returns head state for eth_call at a past block. For pool 0x05db4949 at block 0x3031210 it answered price 0x44eec095... and lastFee 2519, the same as at latest, while rpc.purroofgroup.com answered 0x3c6dac33... and lastFee 3007 (0xbb7), which fits the Swap log. The unit used rpc.purroofgroup.com and is not affected.

leads.question: Does any cleared item or finding for chain 999 depend on eth_call, eth_getStorageAt or eth_getBalance at a past block sent to https://rpc.hyperliquid.xyz/evm, the URL in state/networks.json?
leads.why: That endpoint answered eth_call at block 0x3031210 with head state (pool 0x05db4949 globalState equal to latest), while the archive node rpc.purroofgroup.com answered the parent-block state that fits the Swap log. A historical read through the networks.json URL can return a wrong value without an error. The A10 opcode battery reads are block independent and not affected.
